items.text: COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause:
AN ACT in relation to directing the commissioner of education, in consultation
with the commissioner of health and the comptroller, to study and prepare a
report concerning school insurance reserve funds; and providing for the repeal
of such provisions upon expiration thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6876

SPONSOR: JORDAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act in relation to directing the commissioner of education, in
consultation with the commissioner of health and the comptroller, to
study and prepare a report concerning school insurance reserve funds;
and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 directs the commissioner of education, in consultation with
the commissioner of health and comptroller, to study four issue areas
regarding school insurance reserve funds: the cost to school districts
of maintaining these funds, the cost or savings to their employees, the
impact on healthcare access self-insurance provides, and the amount of
funding set aside for the reserve funds.

Section 2 sets forth the requirements on when the completed study must
be submitted.

Section 3 provides for the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Current law allows municipal corporations to self-insure to provide
health insurance to their employees, officers, and retirees. The general
municipal law allows these municipal corporations to establish and make
expenditures from insurance reserve funds, but exempts accident and
health insurance from these provisions. Previous chapters authorized
specific school districts to use their insurance reserve funds for
expenses related to health and accident insurance.  In the era of the
tax cap, several school districts have opted to adopt self-insurance to
manage rising healthcare costs, and for these districts, insurance
reserve funds are necessary to maintain their self-insurance programs.

In 2019 and 2020 alone, the legislature voted 21 times to add new school
districts to those who are allowed to operate an insurance reserve fund.
As of March 2021, an additional 4 school districts have legislation
before the Senate to gain this authorization. It is clear that self-in-
surance is an option many school districts are interested in pursuing.
This legislation directs the Comptroller to study these reserve funds,
including the typical annual cost of maintaining them, the costs to
employees of school districts who self-insure, the impact on healthcare
access, and the amount of funding that participating districts have set
aside for the fund. By requiring this study and answering those critical
questions, this bill would provide clear information on the benefits, if
any, self-insurance would provide to school districts and the taxpayers
they are responsible to.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Minimal.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.
